title: Surveyed gauge beds show that Victorian stream-side water tables lost about 70% of their height above the bed after 1997, but fell below it at only one in four gaining pairs (17 gauges)
abstract: Question: after 1997, did water tables beside Victorian streams fall below the stream bed (stream-groundwater disconnection), which earlier campaign work proposed as a cause of the persistent 20-25% runoff deficit? Approach: we used WMIS stream gauges whose gauge zero and cease-to-flow stage give a surveyed bed level in m AHD, and WMIS bores with AHD water levels, records before 1996 and after 2010, within 1 km (primary) or 2 km. We then used these surveyed values to check DEM height-above-drainage methods (Copernicus GLO-90, and the GA DEM-H values of SCI d8cf8c14). Results: within 1 km (23 pairs, 10 gauges) the median head was +0.58 m above the bed in 1985-1996 and fell 0.46 m by 2010-2021 (gauge bootstrap 95% interval -1.63 to -0.42 m); 91% of pairs fell. Of pairs above the bed before 1997, 4 of 15 (2 km: 9 of 26) fell below it and none came back, also in 2022-2025. But the height above the bed fell by a median 72% (17-97%), so the head difference that drives groundwater discharge fell by about two thirds, mostly without a crossing. DEM drainage lines were a median 1.2-1.4 m above the surveyed bed (scatter 1.3-2.5 m); the DEM sign agreed with the surveyed sign at only 60-62% of bores, so DEMs cannot show single-bore crossings. Near-stream shallow bores (n=565) fell nearly as much as other bores (0.89 against 1.07 m). A catchment link between near-stream head fall and runoff deficit (21 catchments, partial rho 0.46) reversed with a 20 km2 channel threshold and is not robust. An upper bound on baseflow loss from the head fall (baseflow index x head-excess loss) was 9-11% at three CAMELS gauges, against runoff deficits of 13-66% (AGCD). Conclusion: strict disconnection was local, but the small pre-1997 head excess shrank strongly; this can explain a part of the loss at baseflow-rich streams, not the loss where quickflow dominates. Limitations: 17 gauges, bed surveyed at the gauge control and not next to the bore, deep bore screens, Victoria only, several tests post hoc.
